subject.title: fix(cli): reject unknown models in config set

question: Should `openclaw config set` reject changed text-model references whenever they cannot resolve using the currently available provider catalog and auth-profile state, instead of preserving the prior deferred runtime failure?
rationale: The code is mechanically coherent and has focused proof, but this deliberately changes the upgrade and operational contract for existing config-write workflows during provider/catalog/auth unavailability.

options.title: Accept set-time rejection
options.body: Approve the fail-closed write contract so unknown or currently unresolvable changed text-model references leave the active config unchanged and fail with an actionable CLI error.

options.title: Preserve deferred writes
options.body: Keep the current write behavior and require a different, explicitly scoped product design if validation must not make catalog/auth availability a config-set prerequisite.

recommendation.title: Accept set-time rejection
recommendation.body: Approve the fail-closed write contract so unknown or currently unresolvable changed text-model references leave the active config unchanged and fail with an actionable CLI error.

likelyOwner.reason: This member explicitly characterized the remaining blocker as the maintainer compatibility decision.
